verses.text: One Sabbath, Jesus went to eat at the home of a Pharisee leader. The people there were watching him closely.
A man with swelling was right in front of him.
Jesus asked the legal experts and Pharisees, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath or not?”
They stayed silent. Jesus took the man, healed him, and sent him on his way.
Jesus asked them, “If your son or your ox fell into a well on the Sabbath, wouldn’t you pull him out right away?”
They had no answer to that.
Jesus noticed how the invited guests picked the places of honor, so he told them this parable:
“When someone invites you to a wedding feast, don’t grab the seat of honor. Someone more important than you might have been invited too,”
“and then your host will come over and say, ‘Give this person your seat.’ You’d have to move down to the lowest place, embarrassed.”
“Instead, when you’re invited, go sit in the lowest place. Then your host may say, ‘Friend, come sit higher.’ You’ll be honored in front of everyone at the table.”
“Everyone who lifts themselves up will be brought low, and everyone who humbles themselves will be lifted up.”
Jesus also told the host, “When you put on a lunch or dinner, don’t invite just your friends, brothers, relatives, or rich neighbors. They may invite you back, and you’ll get paid back.”
“Instead, when you host a feast, invite the poor, people with disabilities, those unable to walk, and the blind.”
“Then you’ll be blessed, because they can’t repay you. You’ll be repaid when the righteous are raised.”
One of the people eating with Jesus heard this and said, “Blessed is everyone who will feast in God’s Kingdom!”
Jesus replied, “A man prepared a great dinner and invited many people.”
“When dinner was ready, he sent his servant to tell the guests, ‘Come, everything’s ready now.’”
“But they all started making excuses. The first said, ‘I bought a field, and I need to go see it. Please excuse me.’”
“Another said, ‘I bought five pairs of oxen, and I’m going to try them out. Please excuse me.’”
“Another said, ‘I just got married, so I can’t come.’”

“The servant came back and reported everything. The angry homeowner told him, ‘Hurry out to the city streets and alleys, and bring in the poor, people with disabilities, people who can’t walk, and people who are blind.’”
“The servant said, ‘Sir, I’ve done what you ordered, and there’s still room.’”
“The master said, ‘Go out to the roads and hedges, and urge people to come in so my house will be full.’”
“I’m telling you, none of those first guests will taste my dinner. Many are called, but few are chosen.”
Large crowds were traveling with Jesus. He turned and said to them:
“If anyone comes to me and doesn’t disregard their father, mother, wife, children, brothers, sisters, and even their own life, they can’t be my disciple.”
“Whoever doesn’t carry their own cross and follow me can’t be my disciple.”
“Suppose one of you wants to build a tower. Won’t you first sit down and work out the cost, to see if you can finish it?”
“Otherwise, after laying the foundation, you might not be able to finish. Everyone who sees it will start mocking you,”
“saying, ‘This person started building but couldn’t finish.’”
“Or suppose a king is going to war against another king. Won’t he first sit down and consider whether ten thousand soldiers can face an army of twenty thousand?”
“If he can’t, while the other king is still far away, he’ll send messengers to ask for peace terms.”
“In the same way, none of you can be my disciple unless you give up everything you have.”
“Salt is good, but if it loses its flavor, how can you make it salty again?”
“It’s no good for the soil or even the manure pile. People throw it out. If you have ears to hear, listen!”
